newsitem.title: SPAIN: New allegations revive Spain's bugging scandal.
newsitem.headline: New allegations revive Spain's bugging scandal.

text.p: A Spanish newspaper revived a bugging scandal that rocked Spain with accusations on Monday that the secret service regularly recorded private conversations of King Juan Carlos under the previous Socialist administration.

The Spanish daily El Mundo said a judge had discovered a list belonging to a former official in the military intelligence service CESID which included reference to a recording of a 1984 conversation of the Spanish monarch.
It said the list proved former deputy prime minister Narcis Serra had lied to parliament when he said the king had been bugged only once.

Serra denied on Monday that the king's telephone conversations had been regularly tapped under the government of former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez and said the report was part of a campaign of defamation and blackmail.

Revelations that rogue secret agents tapped the telephones of leading politicians, businessmen and King Juan Carlos prompted the resignation of Serra and then defence minister Julian Garcia Vargas in June 1995.
Serra said the El Mundo report was either invented or false, but added there was a possibility tapes could have been made independently and without knowledge of senior CESID officials.
